name: reference-shell-adapter
description: ARCHIVED worked example of the enforced-spawn binding contract. Parked / not wired in — moa's active model is the learned tool profile (see moa-core/references/learn-tool.md). Targets one concrete CLI as its illustrative runtime; the command names/flags in adapter.py are example, not normative.

notes: The example runtime enforces per-tool whitelists via a tool-allowlist flag, blocks skills/extensions, and disallows network when the allowlist omits browser/web_search.

Bash is a single coarse tool in the example runtime; per-argv allowlisting inside bash is not enforceable, so policies with `bash.argv_allowlist` are downgraded to `sandbox` (it offers bash or no-bash, not filtered bash).
No real process-level isolation (worktree/cgroup/sandbox-fs) — files outside the worker's cwd are not blocked by the runtime, so policies with `filesystem: worktree_copy` are downgraded to `sandbox`.
